Noor (Eng): Ran into a long train strike delay on my transit to Berlin summit. Had to book a last-minute hotel and three extra meals. Can I expense the extra night + meals? What qualifies as per-diem vs exception?

Sasha (People Ops): Sorry that happened! Short answer: if delay caused by carrier (strike, cancellation) and you were traveling on company-approved trip, we cover reasonable additional lodging and meals. Policy prefers per-diem for meals but exceptions allowed for actuals with receipts.

Noor (Eng): Cool. I have hotel receipt, 3 meal receipts (breakfast/lunch/dinner), and the train cancellation email. I booked on my card. Any limits I should know?

Liam (Finance): Need: itemized hotel folio, all meal receipts, proof of delay/cancellation (email screenshot or carrier notice), and manager approval. Meals under $25 can be aggregated but receipts are still best. If total meals exceed local per-diem by >30%, route as exception with manager note.

Priya (Legal): Add: keep documentation showing carrier fault (strike/cancellation). If the vendor offers compensation or vouchers, include that EOD so we don't double-pay. Also confirm no visa/immigration consequences for extended stay in the documentation if that matters.

Noor (Eng): Manager (Diego) already approved in Slack and I attached the carrier email to the expense. Hotel was 88.50, meals totaled 0.40, 0.10, 9.60. Should I pick "actuals" in Expensify or use per-diem?

Sasha (People Ops): Use "actuals" for the hotel and meals since you have receipts. In the expense notes, add: "Train strike on 2026-06-12 caused overnight stay; carrier cancellation email attached; manager approved."

Liam (Finance): We'll process as an exception claim. If the total meal spend looks unreasonable we may ask for a short justification, but these numbers look fine. Expect reimbursement on next run; mark urgent if you need off-cycle.

Noor (Eng): Not urgent, next run is fine. Thanks!

expense-bot: :white_check_mark: Expense submitted (ID EXP-5128). Status: pending finance review.

Sasha (People Ops): Policy note: extraordinary travel disruptions (carrier strikes, natural disaster) qualify for exception reimbursements when documented; always attach carrier proof + manager approval within 60 days.

Liam (Finance): Closing loop: I'll check for carrier compensation. If they issue a voucher later that covers hotel/meals, we'll offset accordingly and reconcile with Noor.

Noor (Eng): Got it, will keep an eye on voucher emails and update the expense if anything comes through. Thanks!
